curriculumDescription: Master C++ from the ground up with interactive byte-sized challenges.

modules.title: Module 1: C++ Basics & Console Output
modules.description: Learn how to send text to your screen using the C++ standard output stream.

cards.instruction: Direct the greeting text into the standard output stream.
cards.concept: In C++, std::cout acts like your computer screen. We use stream insertion arrows to push text onto it.
cards.code: [hint:std::cout|Standard output stream. Think of this as your computer screen.] [blank] [hint:"Welcome!":String literal. Text wrapped in double quotes.] [hint:;:Semicolon. Ends the statement like a period in a sentence.];
cards.explanation: The << arrows point to the left, pushing data directly into the std::cout screen. The >> arrows are used for reading input with std::cin.

cards.instruction: Add a new line after printing your message.
cards.concept: std::endl moves the cursor to the next line on the screen and flushes the output buffer.
cards.code: std::cout << "Hello World!" << [blank] [hint:;:Semicolon ends this C++ command.];
cards.explanation: std::endl stands for 'end line'. It starts a new line on the screen.

cards.instruction: Complete the preprocessor directive to include input-output tools.
cards.concept: Before using std::cout, you must include the input-output stream library header.
cards.code: [hint:#include|Preprocessor directive that includes external libraries before compiling.] <[blank]>
cards.explanation: iostream stands for Input Output Stream. It gives C++ access to std::cout and std::cin.

cards.instruction: Every C++ program starts inside the main entry point function.
cards.concept: The main function returns an integer code to the operating system when it finishes.
cards.explanation: In standard C++, the main function must return an integer type (int) indicating success or failure to the operating system.

modules.title: Module 2: Variables & Fundamental Types
modules.description: Store whole numbers, decimal values, and true/false states in memory.

cards.instruction: Choose the type keyword to store whole numbers.
cards.concept: C++ is strongly typed. You must declare what kind of data a variable holds before using it.
cards.code: [blank] [hint:playerScore|Variable name holding the player's total points.] = 100;
cards.explanation: int is the standard C++ keyword for integer numbers like -5, 0, and 100.

cards.instruction: Declare a decimal number with high precision.
cards.concept: Floating-point numbers can hold fractions and decimal points.
cards.code: [blank] [hint:itemPrice|Variable name storing the price of an item.] = 19.99;
cards.explanation: double provides double-precision floating-point numbers, ideal for numbers with decimal values.

cards.instruction: Read user input from the keyboard into a variable.
cards.concept: std::cin uses extraction arrows pointing to the right to place input into a variable.
cards.code:
int userAge;
[hint:std::cin|Standard input stream that reads keys typed by the user.] [blank] userAge;
cards.explanation: The >> operator points right, extracting data from std::cin and saving it into userAge.

cards.instruction: Store a single letter or character.
cards.concept: Single characters use the char type and must be surrounded by single quotes.
cards.explanation: char stores a single 1-byte character enclosed in single quotes like 'A' or 'z'.

modules.title: Module 3: Conditionals & Decisions
modules.description: Make smart decisions in your code using comparison operators and boolean logic.

cards.instruction: Check if two values are exactly equal.
cards.concept: In C++, a single = assigns a value, while double == checks if two values match.
cards.explanation: Use == to test for equality. A single = will accidentally overwrite the value instead of comparing it.

cards.instruction: Require BOTH conditions to be true using the logical AND operator.
cards.concept: Logical operators combine multiple true/false checks into one decision.
cards.explanation: && is the logical AND operator. It only evaluates to true if both conditions are satisfied.

cards.instruction: Provide a fallback branch when the if check evaluates to false.
cards.concept: The else block executes only when the preceding if test is not true.
cards.explanation: The else keyword marks the code that runs when the if condition evaluates to false.

modules.title: Module 4: Loops & Repetition
modules.description: Run code repeatedly without repeating yourself using for and while loops.

cards.instruction: Complete the loop header to count from 0 up to 4.
cards.concept: A for loop specifies an initializer, a stopping condition, and an increment step.
cards.explanation: i < 5 keeps the loop running while i is 0, 1, 2, 3, and 4, then stops when i reaches 5.

cards.instruction: Increase the loop counter by 1 in every iteration.
cards.concept: The ++ increment operator increases the value stored in a variable by exactly one.
cards.explanation: count++ is shorthand in C++ for count = count + 1.

cards.instruction: Keep running a loop while health is greater than zero.
cards.concept: A while loop tests its condition before every pass through the loop body.
cards.explanation: The while keyword repeats the block as long as the test condition remains true.

modules.title: Module 5: Functions & Scope
modules.description: Organize your code into reusable blocks with parameters and return values.

cards.instruction: Send the calculated sum back to the caller.
cards.concept: The return keyword stops execution of the function and provides the output value.
cards.explanation: return hands the value back to wherever the function was called in your program.

cards.instruction: Specify that a function does not return any value.
cards.concept: When a function only performs an action like printing, its return type is void.
cards.explanation: void tells the C++ compiler that this function will not return any data.

cards.instruction: Pass a variable by reference so the function can modify the original variable.
cards.concept: Placing an & after the type lets the function work directly on the original memory.
cards.explanation: int& creates a reference parameter, allowing the function to modify the caller's actual variable.

modules.title: Module 6: Pointers & Memory Addresses
modules.description: Master computer memory, addresses, and pointer dereferencing in modern C++.

cards.instruction: Get the physical memory address of a variable.
cards.concept: The address-of operator & returns the location in RAM where a variable is stored.
cards.explanation: The & symbol before a variable gets its memory address so a pointer can store it.

cards.instruction: Dereference the pointer to change the value it points to.
cards.concept: The asterisk * before a pointer accesses the actual value stored at that address.
cards.explanation: *ptr dereferences the pointer, allowing you to read or write the value at the address.

cards.instruction: Set an empty pointer safely using modern C++ standards.
cards.concept: Modern C++ uses nullptr instead of the old C-style NULL or 0.
cards.explanation: nullptr is type-safe and prevents accidental integer conversion errors in C++.

modules.title: Module 7: Classes & Object-Oriented C++
modules.description: Model real-world objects using classes, constructors, and encapsulation.

cards.instruction: Make class members accessible from outside the class.
cards.concept: By default, class members are private. The public: label allows outside access.
cards.explanation: public: makes members available to any code that uses an instance of the class.

cards.instruction: Create an instance of the Player class and call its heal method.
cards.concept: Use the dot . operator to access public members of an object instance.
cards.explanation: Use the dot . operator to call methods or access properties on an object instance.

cards.instruction: Define a constructor that runs automatically when an object is created.
cards.concept: A constructor has the exact same name as the class and has no return type.
cards.explanation: A constructor method must share the exact same name as its enclosing class with no return type.
